reason: The repeat-incident briefing goes straight at the pages that woke me up last quarter, but I'm not piping our Slack, GitHub and Drive into an early-preview hosted service from a startup with no SOC 2 or DPA mentioned. At most I'd have someone spin up the MIT self-hosted version on a sandbox repo, and that isn't paying anyone.
objection: This thing would hold every incident, decision and owner across our whole org, which makes it a goldmine if it leaks, and an early-preview cloud from a small vendor won't get through my security review.
would_change_my_mind: A SOC 2 Type II report, a signed DPA and a completed security questionnaire for the managed cloud, or a supported enterprise self-hosted tier with SSO and audit logs that keeps every byte inside our VPC.
